result.summary: The pedestrian environment consists of continuous sidewalks on both sides of a two-lane roadway with parallel parking. The lack of a physical buffer between the walkway and traffic, combined with wide lanes and several boarded-up building frontages, creates a moderately exposed environment for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Wide travel lanes
hazards.description: The width of the travel lanes and the straight geometry of the road likely encourage vehicle speeds higher than appropriate for an urban pedestrian environment.

hazards.name: Lack of pedestrian buffer
hazards.description: Pedestrians on the sidewalk have no physical or vertical separation from moving traffic, increasing the risk of vehicle-pedestrian conflict.
hazards.location_in_image: Both sides of the street, adjacent to the curb

hazards.name: Blank and boarded frontages
hazards.description: Boarded-up windows and vacant lots reduce passive surveillance and 'eyes on the street,' which can impact perceived and actual pedestrian safety.
hazards.location_in_image: Left and right sides of the street

interventions.title: Lane Narrowing
interventions.description: Reduce the width of travel lanes to encourage slower driving speeds and reclaim space for pedestrian improvements.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Furniture Zone
interventions.description: Install street trees or a furniture zone to provide a physical and psychological buffer between the sidewalk and the roadway.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at the nearest intersections to reduce crossing distances and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

result.summary: The image shows a wide concrete sidewalk adjacent to a large industrial building with a blank blue corrugated metal facade. While the walkway is clear and unobstructed, the environment is characterized by a lack of pedestrian-scale amenities, street trees, or buffers from the roadway.

hazards.name: Blank Frontage
hazards.description: The long, windowless industrial wall creates a 'dead' street environment with no natural surveillance, which can decrease perceived safety for pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the image, extending across the entire building facade.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Buffer
hazards.description: There is no physical or vertical separation (like trees or a planting strip) between the wide sidewalk and the roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curb line at the bottom of the image.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Landscaping
interventions.description: Install a planting strip or street trees between the sidewalk and the curb to provide a physical and psychological buffer from traffic.

interventions.title: Pedestrian-Scale Lighting
interventions.description: Add dedicated street-level lighting poles to improve visibility and safety at night, as current lighting is limited to building-mounted fixtures.

result.summary: The street features continuous sidewalks on both sides, but the pedestrian environment is compromised by a lack of marked crossings and physical obstructions. A large utility vehicle is parked directly on the right-side walkway, forcing pedestrians into the roadway, while the wide, straight lanes and lack of traffic calming may encourage higher vehicle speeds.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstruction
hazards.description: A white utility truck is parked directly on the sidewalk on the right side of the image, completely blocking the pedestrian path.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Crossings
hazards.description: There are no marked crosswalks or pedestrian warning signs visible along this stretch of road, increasing risk for mid-block crossings.

interventions.title: Marked Midblock Crossing
interventions.description: Install a high-visibility marked crosswalk with appropriate signage to provide a safe crossing point for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Implement curb extensions (bulb-outs) to shorten crossing distances and prevent vehicles from parking on or near the sidewalk area.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Furniture Zone
interventions.description: Add a planting strip or street trees to create a physical and psychological buffer between the sidewalk and moving traffic.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment consists of a continuous, paved sidewalk directly adjacent to a two-lane roadway without a physical buffer or street trees. The streetscape is characterized by buildings with boarded-up windows and a lack of active frontage, which reduces natural surveillance and pedestrian comfort.
